From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter
Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of
Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and
look forward to your mark-up.
SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)
Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims
is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.
Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and
only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the
basket is recoverable.
Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after
Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims
unless expressly stated otherwise.
Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same
caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.
Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and
non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.
Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public
registers (see Disclosure Letter).
Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the
Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or
public records.
Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller
will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the
counterparty's written consent.
Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding)
will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.
Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing
bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds
flow.)
Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio
matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.
Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter
and is not expected to be material.
Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course
operating costs.
Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime
above.
Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.
Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and
records are fictional.
1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the
indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including
DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly
searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific
disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent,
payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.
2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause
11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final
written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.
3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2.
As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security
is included.
4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of
every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of
non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject
to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft
Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or
on-costs apply.
6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external
email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity
timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised
person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation
remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no
loss amount.
7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as
a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.
8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each

each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

consent is required merely because shares are sold.
10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of
the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the
Buyer has completed its own verification.
11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer
must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-Side Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics; AUD 24,000,000; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law
**Caveat:** I have not seen the full SPA text, only the Seller's summary of its positions and the Disclosure Letter. Clause references follow the Seller's numbering. Statutory points should be confirmed by NSW counsel before they go into the mark-up.

---

## 1. Overall assessment

The package is not "fair and balanced." Its main features are these:

1. **The cover note contradicts the Disclosure Letter.** The cover note says Bluefen is "addressed", Riverlark will be handled by a later release, DD-006 is "not material", and Sandbar is "ordinary course." The Seller's own Disclosure Letter says the Bluefen consent has not been obtained, the facility has not been repaid, the incident investigation is preliminary, and nothing establishes whether the Sandbar renewals are ordinary course. **We should rely on the Disclosure Letter and the data room, not the cover note's characterisations.**
2. **Three provisions together leave us with no remedy for the risks we already know about:**
   - general disclosure of the whole data room and public records (Sch 7, DL 1.1–1.2);
   - a buyer-knowledge bar that includes constructive knowledge (cl 8.3);
   - limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses that apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5, plus the cl 12.3/13 "applies to all Claims" proposal).

   Every issue identified in due diligence would be disclosed, known, and capped. The protections for these risks would only exist on paper.
3. **Quantified exposure nearly equals the proposed cap.** Riverlark (AUD 3.2m), bonuses (AUD 0.42m plus on-costs), Ironquay (AUD 0.18m plus IP risk) and Sandbar (AUD 0.33m) total about **AUD 4.13m** before the privacy incident or any loss of Bluefen. The general cap is AUD 4.8m and would be shared with every unknown warranty claim.

---

## 2. Limitation regime

### 2.1 Fundamental warranties under the general cap and time limit. **Reject.**
The Seller wants capacity and title warranties capped at AUD 4.8m with an 18-month notification period, "for administrative simplicity." This is a substantive concession, not an administrative one. If title or capacity fails, we have paid AUD 24m for shares we may not own.

- **Push for:** title, capacity and authority warranties capped at **100% of the purchase price**, with a time limit of at least **6 years**. That matches the contract limitation period under the *Limitation Act 1969* (NSW). Consider 12 years if the SPA is executed as a deed.
- Fundamental warranties should not be subject to the de minimis, the basket, disclosure (other than express specific disclosure) or the knowledge bar.

### 2.2 "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." **Reject.**
This reverses the normal default. Unless every carve-out is drafted perfectly, it would cap and time-bar specific indemnities, covenant breaches, leakage, price-adjustment and completion-accounts claims, and tax.

- **Push for:** limitations apply **only to Warranty Claims** unless expressly extended. They should be expressly excluded from:
  - fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment (by the Seller, its officers, or Company management before Completion);
  - fundamental warranties;
  - tax warranties and the tax indemnity;
  - specific indemnities (see Part 4);
  - breaches of pre-Completion conduct and Completion covenants;
  - completion accounts and price adjustment.

### 2.3 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance for "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5). **Reject as drafted.**
- **Fraud carve-out is essential.** A clause excluding liability for fraud is commercially unacceptable and of doubtful effect, so we should state the carve-out expressly rather than litigate it.
- Accept non-reliance only for **pre-contractual statements outside the SPA, the Disclosure Letter and the replies to written due diligence questions**. Ask NSW counsel to confirm how the clause interacts with the misleading or deceptive conduct prohibition in the Australian Consumer Law (s 18). A broad non-reliance clause will be used to argue that we did not rely on statements made in diligence.
- Exclusive remedy must not displace specific performance, injunctions, termination rights before Completion, or indemnities.

### 2.4 Cap, de minimis and basket. **Negotiate.**
- **Cap (20%, AUD 4.8m):** within the market range for general warranties, but only acceptable if the known risks sit **outside** it. If we do not take W&I insurance, push for 30–40%. If we do take W&I, the Seller's cap can come down, but **W&I will exclude known issues**. That makes the specific indemnities and escrow in Part 4 more important, not less.
- **De minimis (AUD 25k):** push for AUD 10k–15k, and require related claims arising from the same facts to be **aggregated** when testing the de minimis.
- **Basket (AUD 250k, excess only):** this is a deductible, so we absorb the first AUD 250k every time. Push for a **tipping basket**, where we recover from the first dollar once the threshold is crossed, at around **AUD 120k (0.5%)**.

### 2.5 Time limits. **Negotiate.**
- 18 months is acceptable for general warranties if it covers at least one full audit cycle after Completion. Confirm this against the FY27 audit timetable.
- **Tax warranties and tax indemnity** are not "settled under the general regime." They need a separate period aligned to the ATO amendment period, with **at least 4–5 years** and no limit for fraud or evasion.
- **IP warranties** should run longer than 18 months, at least 3 years, given the Ironquay issue.

---

## 3. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

### 3.1 General disclosure of the data room and public registers (Sch 7; DL 1.1–1.2). **Reject.**
Disclosing "every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in" the data room makes the warranties almost worthless. The phrase "referred to" is particularly wide because it reaches documents that are not even in the data room.

- **Push for:** only **specific disclosures in the Disclosure Letter**, made fairly, with enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely effect, and referenced to the warranty concerned.
- If we have to concede something on the data room, limit it to documents **in an agreed, indexed data room USB delivered at signing**, only to the extent the matter is **fairly and specifically disclosed on the face of the document**, and with no "referred to" extension.
- Limit public records disclosure to the results of specified ASIC, PPSR and court searches run on a stated date.
- **Disclosure must not qualify** fundamental warranties, tax warranties or any specific indemnity. State this expressly. Otherwise DL items 2–6 will be argued to defeat the indemnities designed for those same matters.

### 3.2 DL 1.4 (no admission). **Accept with a fix.**
A non-admission clause is acceptable. Add that nothing in the Disclosure Letter limits any indemnity, Completion deliverable or condition precedent.

### 3.3 Buyer knowledge bar (cl 8.3). **Reject.**
This clause bars claims for anything the Buyer **or its advisers** knew, or that was **discoverable** from the data room or public records. In practice that removes every claim for every issue we found in due diligence. It also turns our diligence work into a weapon against us.

- **Preferred position:** an express provision that the Buyer's knowledge, actual or constructive, does not affect any claim.
- **Fallback:** the bar is limited to the **actual knowledge** of a short list of named Wattlebridge deal team individuals (not advisers) of a matter they knew at signing would constitute a breach. It never applies to specific indemnities, fundamental warranties, tax, or fraud.

---

## 4. Specific issues from the Disclosure Letter

### 4.1 Bluefen change-control consent (DD-002; DL 2; cl 3/6.3). **High priority.**
**Facts:** Bluefen accounts for about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (around 30%). Clause 11.2 of the Bluefen contract requires change-control consent, subject to conditions in cl 11.3. **No final written consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied** has been provided.

**Problems with the Seller's position:**
- "Reasonable endeavours" is a weak obligation.
- Treating the condition as satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" would allow a consent that is **conditional, qualified, or on worse terms** (price concessions, a termination right, new security or audit obligations) to satisfy it, even if the cl 11.3 conditions are left outstanding.

**Push for:**
- A **condition precedent** requiring Bluefen's **unconditional written consent**, in a form reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer, with all cl 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived **by Bluefen**. The consent must not amend Bluefen contract terms adversely without the Buyer's consent.
- The condition to be **for the Buyer's benefit only**, so only the Buyer can waive it.
- The Seller to use **all reasonable endeavours** (or best endeavours), with the Buyer having consultation and approval rights over communications with Bluefen.
- A sunset date with a Buyer termination right.
- **Fallback if we are pressed to complete without consent:** a price reduction, deferred consideration or earn-out tied to Bluefen retention, or escrow released only on receipt of consent. A refusal or termination by Bluefen would significantly impair value.

### 4.2 Riverlark Bank facility (DD-003; DL 3; cl 2/7). **High priority.**
**Facts:** about AUD 3.2m outstanding. The facility contains a change-control clause (cl 8.1) and a discharge mechanism (cl 9.2). It has not been repaid and no discharge is in the data room.

**Problems with the Seller's position:**
- A release "following Completion" is incompatible with a debt-free deal.
- The change-control clause may cause Completion itself to trigger default or acceleration.
- Until the security is discharged, the Company's assets, and possibly **the shares themselves**, remain encumbered.

**Push for:**
- The facility to be **repaid at Completion from the purchase price**, under a payout letter from Riverlark confirming the payout figure (including break costs and daily interest) and an undertaking to release.
- **Completion deliverables:** a signed deed of release, PPSR financing change statements or an authority to lodge them, ASIC charge releases if any, and a release of any guarantee or security given by the Company.
- All Riverlark amounts (principal, interest, break costs, fees) defined as **Debt** and deducted dollar for dollar.
- **Check DD-003 for any share mortgage over the Paperbark shares.** If one exists, its release is part of the title deliverables (see 4.9).
- An indemnity for any amount payable to Riverlark after Completion.

### 4.3 Completion bonuses (DD-005; DL 5; funds flow). **High priority.**
**Facts:** AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses, **not in the funds flow**. The Disclosure Letter is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.

**Problem:** the Seller calls these "a matter for the Seller", but **the Company is the employer and bears the legal liability**. Because the bonuses are excluded from the funds flow and some are subject to continued-employment conditions (so payable after Completion), the cost falls on us. On-costs could add a meaningful amount:
- NSW payroll tax;
- PAYG withholding remittance;
- possibly superannuation guarantee, depending on whether the bonuses count as ordinary time earnings. Get advice on this.
- possibly workers' compensation premiums.

**Push for:**
- The bonuses and **all associated employer on-costs** treated as **Transaction Expenses or Debt**, deducted from the price whether they are paid at or after Completion.
- Alternatively, the gross amount plus on-costs **retained or escrowed** from the price and paid out through payroll when the conditions are met.
- A **specific indemnity** for any bonus, on-cost, penalty or interest. Confirm the full list of recipients and the terms, including any change-of-control, accelerated vesting or "good leaver" provisions.

### 4.4 Ironquay IP (DD-004, DD-010; DL 4; cl 11.1). **High priority.**
**Facts:**
- Clause 7.3 of the Ironquay agreement provides that SOW3 Project Materials **do not transfer until every SOW3 fee is paid in cleared funds**.
- DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open.
- There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- The Seller notes that DD-010 does not independently prove non-payment, but it has offered no evidence of payment either.

**Problem:** the risk is not the AUD 180k. **The Company may not own IP it is using.** That could lead to infringement claims, injunctions, redevelopment costs and customer warranty breaches. Bluefen and other customer contracts may contain IP non-infringement warranties. An indemnity limited to "the specific SOW3 payment" addresses the smallest part of the exposure.

**Push for:**
- **Before Completion:** the Seller procures payment of the outstanding fees (at the Seller's cost, or treated as Debt) **and** delivers a **confirmatory IP assignment deed** from Ironquay covering all SOW3 Project Materials, with moral rights consents. Make this a condition precedent or Completion deliverable.
- A **broadened specific indemnity** covering all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or hold the right to use, the SOW3 materials, including third-party and customer claims and replacement costs. It should sit outside the general cap and limitations, with a separate cap of at least an agreed amount and a duration of at least 3–4 years.
- An IP warranty specifically covering contractor-developed IP.

### 4.5 DD-006 export/privacy incident (DL 6; cl 4.6/Sch 6). **High priority. Requires urgent factual follow-up.**
**Facts:**
- A download link was sent to an unintended external address.
- The file may contain about 1,240 records with names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps.
- Access, scope and notification obligations have not been established.
- As at 22 September 2026 the investigation was preliminary.

**Problems with the Seller's position:**
- The Seller calls the incident "not expected to be material", but its own disclosure does not support that conclusion.
- On implied revenue (Bluefen's AUD 3.6m is about 30%, so total revenue is around AUD 12m), the Company is likely above the small business exemption threshold and subject to the *Privacy Act 1988* (Cth), including the **Notifiable Data Breaches scheme**.
- An entity that suspects an eligible data breach generally has **30 days to assess** it. On the dates disclosed, that window has very likely **already passed**. We need to know whether an assessment was completed and documented, and whether OAIC or individuals were notified.
- Customer contracts, possibly including Bluefen, may impose their own short notification deadlines.
- Penalty exposure under the Privacy Act is now significant.

**Push for:**
- **Immediately:** the forensic or investigation report, a log access record showing whether the link was opened, the NDB assessment and its conclusion, all OAIC and customer correspondence, and confirmation of which customers' data was involved.
- A **specific indemnity**, outside the cap, disclosure and knowledge limitations, covering regulatory penalties, investigation and remediation costs, customer claims, contract termination and individual claims arising from the incident.
- **Escrow or retention** until an agreed period passes without a regulatory or customer claim.
- An updated warranty, repeated at Completion, that the Seller has disclosed all facts known about the incident and that no further incidents have occurred.
- If the facts are worse than presented (for example, confirmed access or Bluefen data involved), consider a **condition precedent or MAC-style termination right**.

### 4.6 Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008, DD-011; DL 8). **Medium priority.**
**Facts:** three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 in total). The Disclosure Letter describes them as "related" and asks that they be "read together for timing/scope." It does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Concerns:**
- Splitting one AUD 330k commitment into three AUD 110k contracts is a recognised way to stay under internal approval limits or SPA conduct-of-business thresholds.
- It is unclear whether "related" means related to each other or to the Seller or its associates. A **related-party** relationship would raise leakage and arm's-length concerns.
- The timing relative to signing and the data room cut-off matters for the conduct-of-business covenants.

**Push for:**
- Answers on all of the above: counterparty ownership, signing dates, approvals, term, termination rights, prepaid or accrued status, and business need.
- If the renewals are non-ordinary course, related-party, or not terminable without cost, treat the unavoidable commitment as **Debt**, or require the Seller to procure termination at its own cost before Completion. Otherwise, take a specific indemnity.
- Tighten the conduct-of-business covenant: aggregate related contracts when testing thresholds, and make any related-party arrangement require Buyer consent.

### 4.7 Office lease (DD-007; DL 7). **Low priority.**
The lease requires notification only, not consent. Make giving the notification a **pre-Completion Seller obligation**. Confirm that the lease has no change-of-control termination right or bank guarantee replacement requirement that the Disclosure Letter does not mention.

### 4.8 Mossvale (DD-009; DL 9). **Low priority.**
The lease contains an assignment restriction only. Confirm that the contract has **no change-of-control clause elsewhere**, including in its definitions or termination provisions. Note that the Disclosure Letter carefully says only that "the provision" does not require consent. Obtain a warranty that no material contract is triggered by the share sale except those listed.

### 4.9 Title (DD-012; DL 10). **High priority on the drafting.**
A share register maintained by the Company is evidence of title, but it is not enough on its own.

**Push for:**
- Title warranties that are **uncapped**, or capped at 100% of the price, with a long time limit and no disclosure qualification. See 2.1.
- Completion deliverables: original share certificates (or a lost-certificate indemnity), signed transfers, register updates, and resignations or appointments.
- Pre-signing and pre-Completion **ASIC and PPSR searches** against both the Company and Harbourglass, to confirm the register matches ASIC records and that no security interest, share mortgage or option exists over the shares.
- A warranty that there are **no options, convertible notes, ESOP entitlements or rights to issue shares**. This is especially relevant given the DD-005 bonuses.
- Release of any encumbrance, including any Riverlark share security, at Completion.

### 4.10 Funds flow. **High priority.**
The current funds flow is incomplete. Rebuild it to show:
- headline price;
- less the Riverlark payout to the bank's account;
- less bonuses and on-costs, either retained or paid;
- less any other Debt and Transaction Expenses;
- less the escrow amount;
- plus or minus estimated completion accounts adjustments.

The Seller's net proceeds should be the balance. Require **payout letters and invoices** for every third-party payment.

---

## 5. Further protection: escrow or retention
Given the unresolved items (Bluefen, the privacy incident, Ironquay IP), propose an **escrow or retention from the price**. As an opening position for commercial discussion, AUD 1.5m–2.5m would be reasonable, held for 12–24 months. Release should be staged and tied to:
- Bluefen consent;
- delivery of the Ironquay assignment;
- expiry of a privacy claims period;
- the first post-Completion audit.

The specific indemnities should be recoverable from escrow first. The quantum is a commercial decision for the deal team.

---

## 6. Information requests to send now
1. The final Bluefen consent (or its current draft) and the status of each cl 11.3 condition.
2. The Riverlark payout letter, break cost estimate and the full security list, including any share security.
3. The DD-005 bonus letters, recipient list and employer on-cost calculation.
4. Ironquay proof of payment or confirmation of the outstanding balance, and Ironquay's willingness to sign a confirmatory assignment.
5. The DD-006 forensic report, access logs, NDB assessment, OAIC and customer notifications, and the identity of affected customers.
6. The Sandbar counterparty's ownership, signing and approval records, and termination terms.
7. Full change-of-control review confirmation for all material contracts, including DD-007 and DD-009.
8. Current ASIC and PPSR searches for the Company and the Seller.

---

## 7. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our position | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fundamental/title warranties | Same 20% cap, 18 months | 100% of price; ≥6 years (12 if deed); no disclosure/knowledge qualification | **Critical** |
| 2 | Scope of limitations | Apply to all Claims unless stated | Warranty Claims only; carve out fraud, fundamentals, tax, indemnities, covenants, completion accounts | **Critical** |
| 3 | Non-reliance/exclusive remedy | All Claims of any nature | Express fraud carve-out; limit non-reliance to statements outside SPA/DL/DDQ replies; preserve equitable remedies | **Critical** |
| 4 | General disclosure | Whole data room and public records | Specific, fair disclosure only; no qualification of fundamentals, tax, indemnities | **Critical** |
| 5 | Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) | Actual and constructive, including advisers | Delete; fallback to actual knowledge of named individuals, excluding indemnities | **Critical** |
| 6 | Bluefen (~30% revenue) | Reasonable endeavours; any written consent | Buyer-only CP: unconditional consent, cl 11.3 satisfied, no adverse terms; sunset/termination; price or escrow protection | **Critical** |
| 7 | Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m) | Release after Completion | Payout at Completion from price; deed of release, PPSR/ASIC releases as deliverables; treated as Debt | **Critical** |
| 8 | Bonuses (AUD 420k + on-costs) | Seller's matter; not in funds flow | Treated as Debt/Transaction Expenses including on-costs; retention plus indemnity | **High** |
| 9 | Ironquay IP | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment | Payment plus confirmatory assignment as CP/deliverable; broad IP indemnity outside cap | **High** |
| 10 | DD-006 privacy incident | "Not material" | Full information now; specific indemnity outside cap; escrow; CP/termination if facts worsen | **High** |
| 11 | Funds flow | "Reflects agreed mechanics" | Rebuild to show all Debt, payouts, bonuses and escrow, supported by payout letters | **High** |
| 12 | Title | Register at DD-012 | Uncapped title warranty; ASIC/PPSR verification; certificates; no options/encumbrances | **High** |
| 13 | Sandbar (AUD 330k) | Ordinary course | Diligence on related-party status and splitting; Debt/termination/indemnity; tighten conduct covenants | Medium |
| 14 | Tax/IP warranties | Settled under general regime | Separate tax indemnity, ≥4–5 years; IP warranties ≥3 years | Medium |
| 15 | Cap/de minimis/basket | 20% / AUD 25k / AUD 250k deductible | 30–40% (or W&I-aligned) / AUD 10–15k with aggregation / AUD 120k tipping | Medium |
| 16 | Lease/Mossvale | No consent needed | Seller to give notices pre-Completion; warranty of no other change-of-control triggers | Low |
| 17 | Escrow | None | AUD 1.5–2.5m (commercial call), 12–24 months, staged release | High |

**Recommended negotiating approach:** lead with items 1–7 as non-negotiable structural points. The cover note's characterisations should be challenged directly using the Seller's own Disclosure Letter. Items 13–16 can be traded, but only once the known risks have been ring-fenced through conditions, Debt treatment, specific indemnities and escrow. If we accept the Seller's limitation and disclosure regime as drafted, our protection against the identified exposures, which total around AUD 4m+ before Bluefen and privacy risk, would be effectively nil.

I can turn this into a clause-by-clause mark-up or an issues list for the Seller once we have the full SPA draft.

The Seller's own Disclosure Letter says the Bluefen consent has not been obtained, the facility has not been repaid, the incident investigation is preliminary, and nothing establishes whether the Sandbar renewals are ordinary course. **We should rely on the Disclosure Letter and the data room, not the cover note's characterisations.**
2. **Three provisions together leave us with no remedy for the risks we already know about:**
   - general disclosure of the whole data room and public records (Sch 7, DL 1.1–1.2);
   - a buyer-knowledge bar that includes constructive knowledge (cl 8.3);
   - limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses that apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5, plus the cl 12.3/13 "applies to all Claims" proposal).

   Every issue identified in due diligence would be disclosed, known, and capped. The protections for these risks would only exist on paper.
3. **Quantified exposure nearly equals the proposed cap.** Riverlark (AUD 3.2m), bonuses (AUD 0.42m plus on-costs), Ironquay (AUD 0.18m plus IP risk) and Sandbar (AUD 0.33m) total about **AUD 4.13m** before the privacy incident or any loss of Bluefen. The general cap is AUD 4.8m and would be shared with every unknown warranty claim.

## 2. Limitation regime

### 2.1 Fundamental warranties under the general cap and time limit. **Reject.**
The Seller wants capacity and title warranties capped at AUD 4.8m with an 18-month notification period, "for administrative simplicity." This is a substantive concession, not an administrative one. If title or capacity fails, we have paid AUD 24m for shares we may not own.

- **Push for:** title, capacity and authority warranties capped at **100% of the purchase price**, with a time limit of at least **6 years**. That matches the contract limitation period under the *Limitation Act 1969* (NSW). Consider 12 years if the SPA is executed as a deed.
- Fundamental warranties should not be subject to the de minimis, the basket, disclosure (other than express specific disclosure) or the knowledge bar.

### 2.2 "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." **Reject.**
This reverses the normal default. Unless every carve-out is drafted perfectly, it would cap and time-bar specific indemnities, covenant breaches, leakage, price-adjustment and completion-accounts claims, and tax.

- **Push for:** limitations apply **only to Warranty Claims** unless expressly extended. They should be expressly excluded from:
  - fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment (by the Seller, its officers, or Company management before Completion);
  - fundamental warranties;
  - tax warranties and the tax indemnity;
  - specific indemnities (see Part 4);
  - breaches of pre-Completion conduct and Completion covenants;
  - completion accounts and price adjustment.

### 2.3 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance for "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5). **Reject as drafted.**
- **Fraud carve-out is essential.** A clause excluding liability for fraud is commercially unacceptable and of doubtful effect, so we should state the carve-out expressly rather than litigate it.
- Accept non-reliance only for **pre-contractual statements outside the SPA, the Disclosure Letter and the replies to written due diligence questions**. Ask NSW counsel to confirm how the clause interacts with the misleading or deceptive conduct prohibition in the Australian Consumer Law (s 18). A broad non-reliance clause will be used to argue that we did not rely on statements made in diligence.
- Exclusive remedy must not displace specific performance, injunctions, termination rights before Completion, or indemnities.

### 2.4 Cap, de minimis and basket. **Negotiate.**
- **Cap (20%, AUD 4.8m):** within the market range for general warranties, but only acceptable if the known risks sit **outside** it. If we do not take W&I insurance, push for 30–40%. If we do take W&I, the Seller's cap can come down, but **W&I will exclude known issues**. That makes the specific indemnities and escrow in Part 4 more important, not less.
- **De minimis (AUD 25k):** push for AUD 10k–15k, and require related claims arising from the same facts to be **aggregated** when testing the de minimis.
- **Basket (AUD 250k, excess only):** this is a deductible, so we absorb the first AUD 250k every time. Push for a **tipping basket**, where we recover from the first dollar once the threshold is crossed, at around **AUD 120k (0.5%)**.

### 2.5 Time limits. **Negotiate.**
- 18 months is acceptable for general warranties if it covers at least one full audit cycle after Completion. Confirm this against the FY27 audit timetable.
- **Tax warranties and tax indemnity** are not "settled under the general regime." They need a separate period aligned to the ATO amendment period, with **at least 4–5 years** and no limit for fraud or evasion.
- **IP warranties** should run longer than 18 months, at least 3 years, given the Ironquay issue.

## 3. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

### 3.1 General disclosure of the data room and public registers (Sch 7; DL 1.1–1.2). **Reject.**
Disclosing "every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in" the data room makes the warranties almost worthless. The phrase "referred to" is particularly wide because it reaches documents that are not even in the data room.

- **Push for:** only **specific disclosures in the Disclosure Letter**, made fairly, with enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely effect, and referenced to the warranty concerned.
- If we have to concede something on the data room, limit it to documents **in an agreed, indexed data room USB delivered at signing**, only to the extent the matter is **fairly and specifically disclosed on the face of the document**, and with no "referred to" extension.
- Limit public records disclosure to the results of specified ASIC, PPSR and court searches run on a stated date.
- **Disclosure must not qualify** fundamental warranties, tax warranties or any specific indemnity. State this expressly. Otherwise DL items 2–6 will be argued to defeat the indemnities designed for those same matters.

### 3.2 DL 1.4 (no admission). **Accept with a fix.**
A non-admission clause is acceptable. Add that nothing in the Disclosure Letter limits any indemnity, Completion deliverable or condition precedent.

### 3.3 Buyer knowledge bar (cl 8.3). **Reject.**
This clause bars claims for anything the Buyer **or its advisers** knew, or that was **discoverable** from the data room or public records. In practice that removes every claim for every issue we found in due diligence. It also turns our diligence work into a weapon against us.

- **Preferred position:** an express provision that the Buyer's knowledge, actual or constructive, does not affect any claim.
- **Fallback:** the bar is limited to the **actual knowledge** of a short list of named Wattlebridge deal team individuals (not advisers) of a matter they knew at signing would constitute a breach. It never applies to specific indemnities, fundamental warranties, tax, or fraud.

## 4. Specific issues from the Disclosure Letter

### 4.1 Bluefen change-control consent (DD-002; DL 2; cl 3/6.3). **High priority.**
**Facts:** Bluefen accounts for about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (around 30%). Clause 11.2 of the Bluefen contract requires change-control consent, subject to conditions in cl 11.3. **No final written consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied** has been provided.

**Problems with the Seller's position:**
- "Reasonable endeavours" is a weak obligation.
- Treating the condition as satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" would allow a consent that is **conditional, qualified, or on worse terms** (price concessions, a termination right, new security or audit obligations) to satisfy it, even if the cl 11.3 conditions are left outstanding.

**Push for:**
- A **condition precedent** requiring Bluefen's **unconditional written consent**, in a form reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer, with all cl 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived **by Bluefen**. The consent must not amend Bluefen contract terms adversely without the Buyer's consent.
- The condition to be **for the Buyer's benefit only**, so only the Buyer can waive it.
- The Seller to use **all reasonable endeavours** (or best endeavours), with the Buyer having consultation and approval rights over communications with Bluefen.
- A sunset date with a Buyer termination right.
- **Fallback if we are pressed to complete without consent:** a price reduction, deferred consideration or earn-out tied to Bluefen retention, or escrow released only on receipt of consent. A refusal or termination by Bluefen would significantly impair value.

### 4.2 Riverlark Bank facility (DD-003; DL 3; cl 2/7). **High priority.**
**Facts:** about AUD 3.2m outstanding. The facility contains a change-control clause (cl 8.1) and a discharge mechanism (cl 9.2). It has not been repaid and no discharge is in the data room.

**Problems with the Seller's position:**
- A release "following Completion" is incompatible with a debt-free deal.
- The change-control clause may cause Completion itself to trigger default or acceleration.
- Until the security is discharged, the Company's assets, and possibly **the shares themselves**, remain encumbered.

**Push for:**
- The facility to be **repaid at Completion from the purchase price**, under a payout letter from Riverlark confirming the payout figure (including break costs and daily interest) and an undertaking to release.
- **Completion deliverables:** a signed deed of release, PPSR financing change statements or an authority to lodge them, ASIC charge releases if any, and a release of any guarantee or security given by the Company.
- All Riverlark amounts (principal, interest, break costs, fees) defined as **Debt** and deducted dollar for dollar.
- **Check DD-003 for any share mortgage over the Paperbark shares.** If one exists, its release is part of the title deliverables (see 4.9).
- An indemnity for any amount payable to Riverlark after Completion.

### 4.3 Completion bonuses (DD-005; DL 5; funds flow). **High priority.**
**Facts:** AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses, **not in the funds flow**. The Disclosure Letter is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.

**Problem:** the Seller calls these "a matter for the Seller", but **the Company is the employer and bears the legal liability**. Because the bonuses are excluded from the funds flow and some are subject to continued-employment conditions (so payable after Completion), the cost falls on us. On-costs could add a meaningful amount:
- NSW payroll tax;
- PAYG withholding remittance;
- possibly superannuation guarantee, depending on whether the bonuses count as ordinary time earnings. Get advice on this.
- possibly workers' compensation premiums.

**Push for:**
- The bonuses and **all associated employer on-costs** treated as **Transaction Expenses or Debt**, deducted from the price whether they are paid at or after Completion.
- Alternatively, the gross amount plus on-costs **retained or escrowed** from the price and paid out through payroll when the conditions are met.
- A **specific indemnity** for any bonus, on-cost, penalty or interest. Confirm the full list of recipients and the terms, including any change-of-control, accelerated vesting or "good leaver" provisions.

### 4.4 Ironquay IP (DD-004, DD-010; DL 4; cl 11.1). **High priority.**
**Facts:**
- Clause 7.3 of the Ironquay agreement provides that SOW3 Project Materials **do not transfer until every SOW3 fee is paid in cleared funds**.
- DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open.
- There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- The Seller notes that DD-010 does not independently prove non-payment, but it has offered no evidence of payment either.

**Problem:** the risk is not the AUD 180k. **The Company may not own IP it is using.** That could lead to infringement claims, injunctions, redevelopment costs and customer warranty breaches. Bluefen and other customer contracts may contain IP non-infringement warranties. An indemnity limited to "the specific SOW3 payment" addresses the smallest part of the exposure.

**Push for:**
- **Before Completion:** the Seller procures payment of the outstanding fees (at the Seller's cost, or treated as Debt) **and** delivers a **confirmatory IP assignment deed** from Ironquay covering all SOW3 Project Materials, with moral rights consents. Make this a condition precedent or Completion deliverable.
- A **broadened specific indemnity** covering all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or hold the right to use, the SOW3 materials, including third-party and customer claims and replacement costs. It should sit outside the general cap and limitations, with a separate cap of at least an agreed amount and a duration of at least 3–4 years.
- An IP warranty specifically covering contractor-developed IP.

### 4.5 DD-006 export/privacy incident (DL 6; cl 4.6/Sch 6). **High priority. Requires urgent factual follow-up.**
**Facts:**
- A download link was sent to an unintended external address.
- The file may contain about 1,240 records with names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps.
- Access, scope and notification obligations have not been established.
- As at 22 September 2026 the investigation was preliminary.

**Problems with the Seller's position:**
- The Seller calls the incident "not expected to be material", but its own disclosure does not support that conclusion.
- On implied revenue (Bluefen's AUD 3.6m is about 30%, so total revenue is around AUD 12m), the Company is likely above the small business exemption threshold and subject to the *Privacy Act 1988* (Cth), including the **Notifiable Data Breaches scheme**.
- An entity that suspects an eligible data breach generally has **30 days to assess** it. On the dates disclosed, that window has very likely **already passed**. We need to know whether an assessment was completed and documented, and whether OAIC or individuals were notified.
- Customer contracts, possibly including Bluefen, may impose their own short notification deadlines.
- Penalty exposure under the Privacy Act is now significant.

**Push for:**
- **Immediately:** the forensic or investigation report, a log access record showing whether the link was opened, the NDB assessment and its conclusion, all OAIC and customer correspondence, and confirmation of which customers' data was involved.
- A **specific indemnity**, outside the cap, disclosure and knowledge limitations, covering regulatory penalties, investigation and remediation costs, customer claims, contract termination and individual claims arising from the incident.
- **Escrow or retention** until an agreed period passes without a regulatory or customer claim.
- An updated warranty, repeated at Completion, that the Seller has disclosed all facts known about the incident and that no further incidents have occurred.
- If the facts are worse than presented (for example, confirmed access or Bluefen data involved), consider a **condition precedent or MAC-style termination right**.

### 4.6 Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008, DD-011; DL 8). **Medium priority.**
**Facts:** three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 in total). The Disclosure Letter describes them as "related" and asks that they be "read together for timing/scope." It does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Concerns:**
- Splitting one AUD 330k commitment into three AUD 110k contracts is a recognised way to stay under internal approval limits or SPA conduct-of-business thresholds.
- It is unclear whether "related" means related to each other or to the Seller or its associates. A **related-party** relationship would raise leakage and arm's-length concerns.
- The timing relative to signing and the data room cut-off matters for the conduct-of-business covenants.

**Push for:**
- Answers on all of the above: counterparty ownership, signing dates, approvals, term, termination rights, prepaid or accrued status, and business need.
- If the renewals are non-ordinary course, related-party, or not terminable without cost, treat the unavoidable commitment as **Debt**, or require the Seller to procure termination at its own cost before Completion. Otherwise, take a specific indemnity.
- Tighten the conduct-of-business covenant: aggregate related contracts when testing thresholds, and make any related-party arrangement require Buyer consent.

### 4.7 Office lease (DD-007; DL 7). **Low priority.**
The lease requires notification only, not consent. Make giving the notification a **pre-Completion Seller obligation**. Confirm that the lease has no change-of-control termination right or bank guarantee replacement requirement that the Disclosure Letter does not mention.

### 4.8 Mossvale (DD-009; DL 9). **Low priority.**
The lease contains an assignment restriction only. Confirm that the contract has **no change-of-control clause elsewhere**, including in its definitions or termination provisions. Note that the Disclosure Letter carefully says only that "the provision" does not require consent. Obtain a warranty that no material contract is triggered by the share sale except those listed.

### 4.9 Title (DD-012; DL 10). **High priority on the drafting.**
A share register maintained by the Company is evidence of title, but it is not enough on its own.

**Push for:**
- Title warranties that are **uncapped**, or capped at 100% of the price, with a long time limit and no disclosure qualification. See 2.1.
- Completion deliverables: original share certificates (or a lost-certificate indemnity), signed transfers, register updates, and resignations or appointments.
- Pre-signing and pre-Completion **ASIC and PPSR searches** against both the Company and Harbourglass, to confirm the register matches ASIC records and that no security interest, share mortgage or option exists over the shares.
- A warranty that there are **no options, convertible notes, ESOP entitlements or rights to issue shares**. This is especially relevant given the DD-005 bonuses.
- Release of any encumbrance, including any Riverlark share security, at Completion.

### 4.10 Funds flow. **High priority.**
The current funds flow is incomplete. Rebuild it to show:
- headline price;
- less the Riverlark payout to the bank's account;
- less bonuses and on-costs, either retained or paid;
- less any other Debt and Transaction Expenses;
- less the escrow amount;
- plus or minus estimated completion accounts adjustments.

The Seller's net proceeds should be the balance. Require **payout letters and invoices** for every third-party payment.

## 5. Further protection: escrow or retention
Given the unresolved items (Bluefen, the privacy incident, Ironquay IP), propose an **escrow or retention from the price**. As an opening position for commercial discussion, AUD 1.5m–2.5m would be reasonable, held for 12–24 months. Release should be staged and tied to:
- Bluefen consent;
- delivery of the Ironquay assignment;
- expiry of a privacy claims period;
- the first post-Completion audit.

The specific indemnities should be recoverable from escrow first. The quantum is a commercial decision for the deal team.
